newsitem.title: FRANCE: HORSE RACING-HELISSIO TO STAKE ARC CLAIM ON STAR-STUDDED WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-HELISSIO TO STAKE ARC CLAIM ON STAR-STUDDED WEEKEND.

text.p: Longchamp's star-studded Sunday card features five group races, including three recognised Arc de Triomphe trials -- the Prix Vermeille, Prix Niel and Prix Foy.

Helissio, whose only blemish on an otherwise distinguished record was in the French Derby in June when he pulled too hard, was given a break after taking the group one Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud in good style in July.

Trained specially with the Arc in mind, Helissio gets a further chance to test his glowing reputation in the group two Prix Niel against the likes of the highly regarded Aga Khan colt Darazari, and the English raider Polaris Flight.

Andre Fabre's Swain, third in last year's Arc and second to Helissio in the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud, will need to be at the top of his game if he is lower the colours of the smart British colt Pentire in the group three Prix Foy.
Pentire missed the break and was all of 10 lengths adrift in the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Diamond Stakes at Ascot in July, before coming back to win in the style of a champion.
The group one Prix Vermeille for three-year-old fillies has an open feel to it, with Fabre running Luna Wells, Tulipa and Miss Tahiti.

Luna Wells would be the pick on spring form. However, there have been encouraging reports about Tulipa and last year's Prix Marcel Boussac winner Miss Tahiti, who had Luna Wells back in seventh when second to Sil Sila in the French Oaks in June.
Tulipa, winner of the Ribblesdale Stakes at Royal Ascot in June but unraced since, is capable of more progress and is highly rated.
Bint Salsabil and Papering, second in the Nassau Stakes and the Yorkshire Oaks, look the best of the invaders.

Fabre's Zamindar, a full brother to 1992 champion European juvenile and 1993 2,000 Guineas hero Zafonic, bids to regain the winning thread in the group one Prix de la Salamandre after a shock defeat in the Prix Morny by British colt Bahamian Bounty.
